decisions.rationale: Lead Mega Charizard Y plus Venusaur establishes sun and immediate sleep/Grass pressure into likely Rotom-Wash, Garchomp, and Aegislash structures. Kingambit is reserved for Floette-Eternal, while Raichu supplies fast Fake Out, Talonflame/Rotom pressure, and Lightning Rod utility.
decisions.notebook: Aegislash is Focus Sash, Stance Change, with Wide Guard/Close Combat/Shadow Sneak/King’s Shield; it strongly favored repeated Wide Guard and can threaten Kingambit with Close Combat. Spiritomb is Leftovers Pressure with Foul Play/Will-O-Wisp/Pain Split/Protect and can prolong games through Protect plus Pain Split. Talonflame is Life Orb Gale Wings with Tailwind, Flare Blitz, Brave Bird, and Quick Guard. Garchomp is Lum Berry Rough Skin with Rock Slide/Earthquake/Scale Shot/Protect. Against defensive Aegislash/Spiritomb structures, use Venusaur sleep pressure to disable Wide Guard and use Mega Charizard Y single-target attacks; preserve Kingambit for Floette if brought.

decisions.rationale: Talonflame+Aegislash lead denies sun: Gale Wings Brave Bird plus Shadow Sneak breaks Focus Sash Venusaur before Sleep Powder, while Wide Guard covers Heat Wave/Rock Slide and Quick Guard covers Fake Out/Sucker Punch. Floette and Garchomp back give Mega Fairy cleanup, Sableye answer, Electric immunity, Lum sleep absorber, and Rock Slide/Earthquake pressure.
decisions.notebook: Opp core is Charizard-Y Drought + Focus Sash Chlorophyll Venusaur; Venusaur outspeeds in sun, so remove it before Sleep Powder. Lead plan: Talonflame Brave Bird + Aegislash Shadow Sneak KO sash Venusaur; Talonflame has Gale Wings priority only at full HP, so keep it unhit if Venusaur Protects. Aegislash Wide Guard blocks Heat Wave/Rock Slide; Quick Guard blocks Fake Out/Sucker Punch. Using both guards same turn makes the second 1/3 because Talonflame moves first; prioritize Wide Guard vs sun. Floette mega-evolves: Fairy Aura Moonblast OHKOes Sableye, Psychic finishes Venusaur/Tauros; it is not Grass, so Flower Veil does not block its own sleep. Garchomp is Electric immunity and Lum sleep absorber; Rock Slide Charizard, Earthquake Raichu/Kingambit; switch it in vs Raichu Thunderbolt. Talonflame is 4x weak to Rock and 2x to Electric; keep it away from Tauros Rock Slide and Raichu. Kingambit: Aegislash Close Combat is main answer, but Sucker Punch moves first; use Quick Guard/Protect; avoid lowering its stats because Defiant. Raichu Lightning Rod absorbs Electric; Garchomp/Aegislash/Floette pressure it. Tauros-Aqua Intimidate; Floette special attacks unaffected, Aegislash immune Close Combat. Sableye Prankster status is best answered by Floette; Aegislash cannot hit it. Bench order: Floette then Garchomp as pivots; consider Rotom only if needing Thunderbolt Charizard, Spiritomb only if Sableye is repeated.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve to establish sun and Chlorophyll, then Sleep Powder Aegislash to disrupt its repeated Wide Guard. Air Slash gives meaningful Talonflame chip while it is likely spending the turn setting Tailwind; Heat Wave is too vulnerable to Wide Guard.

Bring Raichu to preserve Kingambit for Floette and retain Lightning Rod pressure against a likely Rotom-Wash pivot. Raichu also provides immediate speed control through Nuzzle while Charizard threatens Aegislash.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Kingambit where possible for Floette-Eternal; it is vulnerable to Aegislash Close Combat. Raichu's Lightning Rod is valuable versus Rotom-Wash, and Nuzzle offers speed control. Aegislash has Focus Sash, Stance Change, Wide Guard, Close Combat, Shadow Sneak, and King's Shield; do not rely on spread Fire attacks through Wide Guard. Talonflame was Life Orb Gale Wings with Tailwind, Flare Blitz, Brave Bird, Quick Guard. Garchomp is Lum Berry Rough Skin with Rock Slide, Earthquake, Scale Shot, Protect. Spiritomb is Leftovers Pressure with Foul Play, Will-O-Wisp, Pain Split, Protect. Against Aegislash/Spiritomb, use Venusaur sleep pressure when available to disrupt Wide Guard and employ Charizard single-target attacks.

decisions.rationale: Brave Bird OHKOes Venusaur down to Focus Sash across all legal spreads; Shadow Sneak's +1 priority then removes the 1 HP before Chlorophyll Venusaur can Sleep Powder. Gale Wings gives Brave Bird priority while Talonflame is full. Charizard's sun Heat Wave afterward cannot KO Talonflame and Focus Sash saves Aegislash, acceptable to remove the sun sweeper.
decisions.notebook: Opp core: Charizard-Y Drought + Focus Sash Chlorophyll Venusaur. Talonflame Brave Bird OHKOes Venusaur to Sash (104-191%); Aegislash Shadow Sneak finishes 1 HP. Gale Wings Flying priority only at full HP; Brave Bird recoil or Heat Wave chip removes it. Charizard-Y sun spread Heat Wave: 38.7-54.8% Talonflame, can OHKO Aegislash but Focus Sash saves from full; Air Slash is 54.8-77.4% Talonflame, so after Brave Bird recoil it can KO. Solar Beam negligible vs Talonflame. Venusaur Sludge Bomb is 49-73.5% Talonflame and immune vs Aegislash. Talonflame Brave Bird vs Charizard-Y is 53.5-102%; Aegislash Shadow Sneak chips 11-22%. Wide Guard blocks Heat Wave/Rock Slide and preserves Gale Wings if Venusaur Protects; Shadow Sneak is the KO option when expecting no Protect. Quick Guard answers Fake Out/Sucker Punch. Garchomp Lum absorbs Sleep Powder and is the Electric immunity; switch vs Raichu Thunderbolt. Floette mega Fairy Aura: Moonblast Sableye, Psychic Venusaur/Tauros; Flower Veil does not block its own sleep. Kingambit: Aegislash Close Combat, beware Sucker Punch and Defiant. Tauros-Aqua Intimidate; special attackers unaffected. Bench order Floette then Garchomp.

decisions.rationale: Bring Floette. It Mega Evolves before moves, survives Charizard single-target hits and Tauros Iron Head (59-88), and OHKOes their likely physical answers Tauros/Sableye with Fairy Aura Moonblast; Aegislash can Wide Guard sun Heat Wave. Garchomp stays in reserve as the Rock Slide check to Charizard-Y and avoids Intimidate. Garchomp now would pressure Zard but is walled by Tauros/Sableye, so Floette maximizes expected value.
decisions.notebook: Opp Charizard-Y Timid sun special attacker: Heat Wave spread vs Garchomp 18-39, vs Mega Floette 33-69; Air Slash/Solar Beam single-target can bypass Wide Guard but do not OHKO either. Garchomp Adamant Rock Slide spread 58-112 vs Charizard (possible OHKO), EQ spread vs Raichu 95-197, vs Kingambit 49-82; Tauros Intimidate and Sableye status make Garchomp a poor first switch into physical-answer leads. Mega Floette (Fairy Aura, SpA 207) Moonblast OHKOes Tauros-Paldea-Aqua and Sableye, possible OHKO Raichu, neutral 52-95 Kingambit; Tauros Iron Head 59-88 and Kingambit Sucker Punch 27-39 do not OHKO Mega Floette, but Kingambit Iron Head does if it gets a turn. Aegislash Focus Sash survives any full-HP hit; Wide Guard blocks Heat Wave/Rock Slide; Fake Out immune vs Aegislash; Close Combat OHKOes Kingambit. Raichu Thunderbolt 22-35 vs Mega Floette; Nuzzle/Fake Out support. Plan: use Floette first to bait/kill Tauros/Sableye/Raichu/Kingambit, keep Garchomp as later Charizard check; use Aegislash Wide Guard/King's Shield to preserve sash and block spread moves; beware Charizard Protect and single-target Air Slash/Solar Beam. Sableye is immune to Close Combat; Floette is primary answer. Kingambit Defiant/Sucker Punch: bait with King's Shield or force with Close Combat when sash intact.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out denies Floette’s Protect, Calm Mind, or attack this turn, while sun-boosted Solar Beam is the strongest available single-target pressure into it and bypasses Aegislash’s Wide Guard. This preserves Raichu’s Lightning Rod utility for Rotom-Wash.
decisions.notebook: Floette-Eternal is Modest Flower Veil with Floettite, Moonblast, Calm Mind, Psychic, and Protect. Solar Beam from Mega Charizard Y is neutral into it and deals roughly 29–52% before any unrevealed effects; Fake Out can deny its first active turn. Aegislash-Blade is Adamant Focus Sash with Wide Guard, Close Combat, Shadow Sneak, and King’s Shield; avoid relying on spread Fire damage when Wide Guard is available. Preserve Kingambit where possible for Floette, but avoid exposing it to Aegislash Close Combat. Raichu’s Lightning Rod is valuable against Rotom-Wash; Nuzzle provides speed control. Garchomp is Lum Berry Rough Skin with Rock Slide, Earthquake, Scale Shot, Protect. Spiritomb is Leftovers Pressure with Foul Play, Will-O-Wisp, Pain Split, Protect.

Preserves full HP on both; next turn Mega Floette threatens Raichu (66-129% Moonblast) with Aegislash support intact.

decisions.rationale: Solar Beam provides the strongest immediate chip into Floette while Raichu’s faster Nuzzle imposes lasting speed control and gives a full-paralysis chance before Floette acts. The double attack cannot reliably KO from full, so Thunderbolt is less valuable than paralysis.
decisions.notebook: Mega Floette is Modest with Fairy Aura, Moonblast, Calm Mind, Psychic, Protect, and Floettite. Charizard-Mega-Y Solar Beam is neutral into it for about 26.5–45.6%; Raichu Thunderbolt is neutral for about 18.2–30.9%, so neither double target is a reliable full-HP KO. Charizard is guaranteed faster than Floette absent speed control. Aegislash-Blade is Adamant Focus Sash with Wide Guard, Close Combat, Shadow Sneak, King’s Shield; do not rely on spread Fire while Wide Guard is available. Preserve Kingambit as a Floette answer while avoiding Aegislash Close Combat. Raichu’s Lightning Rod is important versus Rotom-Wash; Nuzzle offers durable speed control. Garchomp is Lum Berry Rough Skin with Rock Slide, Earthquake, Scale Shot, Protect. Spiritomb is Leftovers Pressure with Foul Play, Will-O-Wisp, Pain Split, Protect.

Solar Beam only does 29-49% to Floette if Charizard bypasses Wide Guard single-target. Focus Sash covers Aegislash vs any single-target hit. Protect is unreliable after last turn's use.

decisions.rationale: Solar Beam is a guaranteed KO on Floette if it does not Protect, and Charizard moves first. Kingambit Protect denies Aegislash’s immediate Close Combat line, preserving the key Steel answer for Floette and avoiding a needless Life Orb attack into King’s Shield.
decisions.notebook: Mega Floette is Modest with Fairy Aura, Moonblast, Calm Mind, Psychic, Protect, and Floettite; it is paralyzed. Charizard-Mega-Y is guaranteed faster than paralyzed Floette absent priority and Solar Beam cleanly finishes it once sufficiently chipped. Aegislash-Blade is Adamant Focus Sash with Wide Guard, Close Combat, Shadow Sneak, King’s Shield; do not rely on spread Fire while Wide Guard is available, and protect Kingambit from Close Combat. Preserve Kingambit as the primary Floette answer. Rotom-Wash has Thunderbolt, Hydro Pump, Will-O-Wisp, Protect with Sitrus Berry and Levitate. Garchomp is Lum Berry Rough Skin with Rock Slide, Earthquake, Scale Shot, Protect. Spiritomb is Leftovers Pressure with Foul Play, Will-O-Wisp, Pain Split, Protect.

decisions.rationale: Floette at 26% is KOed by both Solar Beam (32-45%) and Iron Head (124-178%); Protect is mandatory. Aegislash faces OHKO from Heat Wave, Kowtow Cleave, and Sucker Punch; King's Shield preserves Focus Sash intact. Both +4 priority protections resolve before all foe attacks. Opponent has no bench—stalling sun (2 turns) is safe and optimal. Once sun expires, Solar Beam becomes 2-turn, enabling a safe Garchomp switch to Rock Slide Charizard (78-181% single-target). Series lead 1-0 favors patience.
decisions.notebook: G2 opponent has no bench (only Charizard+Kingambit). Garchomp is 4x weak to Solar Beam—never switch in during sun. After sun expires Solar Beam requires charge turn, enabling safe Garchomp entry. Rock Slide vs Charizard: 58-136% spread, ~78-181% single-target; EQ vs Kingambit 49-82. Aegislash Focus Sash guarantees one survival from full HP; King's Shield preserves sash and baits Sucker Punch. Floette paralyzed (Spd 77) and fragile—Protect essential vs Solar Beam/Iron Head. Wide Guard blocks Heat Wave/Rock Slide; King's Shield blocks all single-target. Strategy: stall sun with Protect+King's Shield, then Garchomp cleanup. Series lead 1-0: play conservatively, preserve Garchomp as Charizard answer. If game 3: expect Sableye/Tauros leads again; Floette is primary answer to both, avoid leading Garchomp into Intimidate/status.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Solar Beam guarantees the KO on Floette if it does not Protect. Kingambit has no needed attack into that line, so Protect is the best attempt to deny Aegislash’s Close Combat; if it fails, Kingambit still survives a noncritical Close Combat and remains the key Steel answer.
decisions.notebook: Mega Floette: Modest, Fairy Aura, Moonblast/Calm Mind/Psychic/Protect, Floettite; paralysis makes it slower than Mega Charizard Y outside priority. Aegislash: Adamant Focus Sash, Wide Guard/Close Combat/Shadow Sneak/King’s Shield. Do not depend on Heat Wave while Wide Guard is available. Kingambit is the main Floette answer, but must respect Close Combat. Rotom-Wash: Modest Sitrus, Levitate, Thunderbolt/Hydro Pump/Will-O-Wisp/Protect. Garchomp: Adamant Lum Rough Skin, Rock Slide/Earthquake/Scale Shot/Protect. Spiritomb: Bold Leftovers Pressure, Foul Play/Will-O-Wisp/Pain Split/Protect. Talonflame: Adamant Life Orb Gale Wings, Tailwind/Flare Blitz/Brave Bird/Quick Guard.

decisions.rationale: Sun's final turn. Floette at 26% is OHKO'd by Iron Head and Solar Beam—Protect is mandatory despite reduced rate. Aegislash King's Shield blocks all single-target threats (Kowtow, Sucker Punch) and punishes contact with -2 Atk, preserving Focus Sash. Close Combat only 54-110% on Kingambit, not a reliable OHKO. Both protect → sun expires → Solar Beam needs charge next turn → safe Garchomp entry. Conservative play with series lead.

Double-target Garchomp with Air Slash plus priority Sucker Punch: this is the only immediate line that can remove the Rock Slide threat before it acts. Sucker Punch is enabled if Garchomp uses its expected attacking options; preserving both foes leaves Charizard exposed to Rock Slide and Kingambit to Close Combat.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Garchomp)
decisions.rationale: Rock Slide hits Charizard 4x SE (65-152%), potentially KOing the biggest threat. Wide Guard blocks Heat Wave, preventing the Heat Wave→Kowtow Cleave combo that would break through Aegislash's Focus Sash. Sucker Punch also fails vs Wide Guard (status move). Garchomp resists Heat Wave anyway (18-26%). If Charizard Air Slashes instead, Garchomp takes manageable 40-55%. Opponent has no bench—applying immediate pressure to Charizard is paramount.
decisions.notebook: G2 confirmed: sun expiry forces Solar Beam charge turn, enabling safe Garchomp entry. Opponent had no bench (Charizard+Kingambit only). Key calcs: Rock Slide vs Charizard 65-152% spread; Heat Wave vs Aegislash 66-93% (no OHKO alone but enables Kowtow follow-up); Kowtow Cleave LO vs Aegislash 97-139%; Sucker Punch LO vs Aegislash 80-116%. Wide Guard blocks Heat Wave and makes Sucker Punch fail vs Aegislash. King's Shield consecutive-use risk after turn 5 success—prefer Wide Guard when spread protection suffices. If game 3: expect Sableye/Tauros-Aqua leads; Floette is primary answer to both (Fairy Aura Moonblast vs Tauros, resists Sableye). Avoid leading Garchomp into Intimidate/status. Tauros has Expert Belt + Intimidate, Rock Slide/Close Combat coverage. Sableye has Prankster Taunt/WillOWisp—Mental Herb. Preserve Garchomp as Charizard answer; never switch into sun Solar Beam. Series lead 1-0: conservative play, protect Garchomp HP.

decisions.rationale: Protect keeps Kingambit safe from Close Combat while Kowtow Cleave reliably threatens to break Aegislash’s Focus Sash through any non-King’s Shield line. Once its Sash is gone, Charizard can finish it safely; Heat Wave remains unusable into Wide Guard.
decisions.notebook: Aegislash is Adamant with Focus Sash, Wide Guard, Close Combat, Shadow Sneak, and King’s Shield. Do not rely on Heat Wave while it is alive. Mega Charizard Y outspeeds it; Close Combat into Charizard is resisted, but it is extremely dangerous to Kingambit. Preserve Kingambit when possible to remove Fairy-types and pressure Ghost/Steel targets. Garchomp is Adamant Lum Berry Rough Skin with Rock Slide/Earthquake/Scale Shot/Protect. Talonflame is Adamant Life Orb Gale Wings. Rotom-Wash is Modest Sitrus Levitate with Thunderbolt/Hydro Pump/Will-O-Wisp/Protect; Spiritomb is Bold Leftovers Pressure with Foul Play/Will-O-Wisp/Pain Split/Protect. Mega Floette is Modest Fairy Aura with Moonblast/Calm Mind/Psychic/Protect.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is fainted, so pass. The game is likely lost, but conceding abandons any slim chance. Aegislash's only meaningful line is Close Combat into Kingambit: 4x super effective and the only move that can immediately remove a threat. Wide Guard blocks only spread moves, King's Shield is unreliable in this protection chain, and Shadow Sneak/Close Combat into Charizard do too little damage.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 plan: opponent likely leads Sableye + Tauros-Paldea-Aqua if they saved them; Floette is primary answer (Fairy Aura Moonblast pressures Tauros, resists Sableye). Avoid leading Garchomp into Intimidate or Prankster status; preserve Garchomp as Charizard answer. Never switch into sun Solar Beam; sun expiry forces Solar Beam charge turn, enabling safe entry. Tauros: Expert Belt, Intimidate, Rock Slide/Close Combat coverage. Sableye: Prankster Taunt/WillOWisp, Mental Herb. Charizard-Mega-Y: Timid special attacker; Heat Wave is spread and can be blocked by Wide Guard, Air Slash/Solar Beam are single-target and not blocked. Solar Beam without sun needs charge. Kingambit: Adamant Life Orb; Kowtow Cleave/Sucker Punch are Dark SE vs Aegislash, Iron Head weak. Aegislash: Focus Sash only saves at full HP; prior chip disables it. Close Combat vs Kingambit is 4x but not guaranteed OHKO on bulky spreads; Shadow Sneak vs Charizard is weak. Protection chain: King's Shield uses 1/X success where X triples after successful protection; Wide Guard does not roll its own success but shares/resets the chain, so King's Shield after Wide Guard is unreliable. Wide Guard blocks only moves targeting all adjacent foes/Pokemon; it does not block single-target moves. Sucker Punch fails if target selects a status move. General series: when ahead, play conservatively and protect remaining win conditions; in lost endgames, prioritize removing one threat over passive protection if any nonzero win chance remains.

decisions.rationale: Air Slash is the only damaging option Aegislash cannot stop with Wide Guard; it also threatens flinches while Charizard outspeeds. Heat Wave is unsafe into its revealed Wide Guard.
decisions.notebook: Aegislash is Adamant Focus Sash with Wide Guard, Close Combat, Shadow Sneak, and King’s Shield. Avoid relying on Heat Wave while it remains alive; Charizard outspeeds and Air Slash bypasses Wide Guard, though King’s Shield must be respected. Mega Charizard Y is Timid with Drought. Garchomp is Adamant Lum Berry Rough Skin with Rock Slide/Earthquake/Scale Shot/Protect. Talonflame is Adamant Life Orb Gale Wings. Rotom-Wash is Modest Sitrus Levitate with Thunderbolt/Hydro Pump/Will-O-Wisp/Protect. Spiritomb is Bold Leftovers Pressure with Foul Play/Will-O-Wisp/Pain Split/Protect. Mega Floette is Modest Fairy Aura with Moonblast/Calm Mind/Psychic/Protect.

Shadow Sneak's priority chips immediately, preserving the tiny chance from Heat Wave misses, crits, or Air Slash misreads, and fits the aggressive lost-endgame heuristic.

Aegislash Focus Sash only saves at full HP; Close Combat defense drops make Charizard Heat Wave lethal even after King's Shield forme. Wide Guard blocks only all-adjacent spread moves, not single-target attacks. In lost endgames, prioritize landing damage with priority over passive protection if any nonzero win chance remains. Against Charizard-Y, prefer Shadow Sneak when Wide Guard can be bypassed by Air Slash.

reflections.summary: Won game 2 and the series 2-0 primarily because Mega Charizard Y plus Raichu/Kingambit gave a workable answer to the opponent’s Mega Floette–Aegislash core: Raichu’s Nuzzle crippled Floette, Charizard’s repeated single-target Solar Beams ignored Aegislash’s Wide Guard, and Kingambit plus Charizard removed Garchomp before it could exploit Rock Slide/Earthquake pressure. The adjustment away from relying on spread damage was effective; Air Slash also correctly finished through Aegislash’s Wide Guard. The bring was broadly well suited: Charizard Y was the right Mega and Venusaur’s sun support was useful in principle, while Raichu provided key speed control. However, Floette’s double Protect bought several turns and Raichu was lost immediately after its utility, so the plan was more fragile than necessary. Prep was strong in registering Charizard Y, Venusaur, Kingambit, Raichu, Tauros-Aqua, and Sableye for this matchup: they offer sun, disruption, Steel pressure, and anti-Water tools. Dragonite, Altaria, Emolga, and Avalugg do not show a clearer matchup advantage from the revealed evidence. The main prep concern is that Venusaur had little demonstrated impact and the team still lacked a particularly clean Aegislash answer once Charizard was exposed to Shadow Sneak.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series, continue to Mega Evolve Charizard Y and prioritize single-target attacks into the Aegislash/Floette structure rather than Heat Wave into known Wide Guard. Lead or bring Raichu when Floette is likely, but use Fake Out more selectively because Floette can Protect; Nuzzle remains valuable for denying Calm Mind/speed control. Preserve Charizard’s HP carefully against Aegislash Shadow Sneak and Garchomp Rock Slide, and avoid leaving it as the sole endgame answer to Aegislash. Consider bringing Tauros-Aqua or Sableye over Venusaur when expecting Rotom-Wash, Talonflame, and physical attackers, since Intimidate or Prankster disruption may provide more reliable value than Venusaur did here. Keep Kingambit for Floette/Garchomp pressure, but do not assume it survives Aegislash Close Combat.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s central revealed core is Mega Floette (Modest, Fairy Aura, Moonblast/Calm Mind/Psychic/Protect) with Adamant Focus Sash Aegislash (Wide Guard/Close Combat/Shadow Sneak/King’s Shield). Floette is willing to use Protect repeatedly to stall sun or scout; pressure it with single-target attacks and speed control before it can Calm Mind. Aegislash repeatedly uses Wide Guard, so avoid making spread damage the primary plan; single-target Charizard attacks are effective, but preserve Charizard from Shadow Sneak. Garchomp is Adamant Lum Rough Skin with Rock Slide/Earthquake/Scale Shot/Protect; Lum limits status-based answers and it must be removed promptly because of Charizard pressure. Talonflame is Adamant Life Orb Gale Wings with Tailwind, Flare Blitz, Brave Bird, Quick Guard. Rotom-Wash is Modest Sitrus with Thunderbolt/Hydro Pump/Will-O-Wisp/Protect; Spiritomb is Bold Leftovers with Foul Play/Will-O-Wisp/Pain Split/Protect. Charizard Y was the correct Mega and a strong matchup piece. Raichu’s Nuzzle was high-value against Floette, while Kingambit provided important Garchomp/Fairy pressure but is vulnerable to Aegislash Close Combat. Consider Tauros-Aqua or Sableye for a more durable disruption slot than Venusaur in this matchup.
